scenes.heading: Experience Fragments (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Templates. Experience Fragments (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is an experience fragment in AEMaaCS?
scenes.heading: A grouped set of components that, when combined, create an experience
scenes.body: An experience fragment in AEMaaCS is a grouped set of components that, when combined, create an experience — for example, a title, image, description, and call-to-action button combined to form a teaser experience.

scenes.question: Where are experience fragments stored, and how are they organized?
scenes.heading: The Experience Fragments Library, organized by categories such as teasers, headers, and footers
scenes.body: Experience fragments are stored in the Experience Fragments Library, a central repository for all experience fragments in an AEMaaCS project, organized by categories such as teasers, headers, and footers.

scenes.question: What are the first steps to create an experience fragment?
scenes.heading: Create a new component in the Experience Fragments Library, add components and properties to it, such as title, description, and image
scenes.body: To create an experience fragment, you first create a new component in the Experience Fragments Library, then add other components to it, along with properties like a title, description, and image.

scenes.question: How do you use an existing experience fragment inside a page or component?
scenes.heading: Add a reference to it via the Component Inspector; AEM creates a new instance inheriting the fragment's properties
scenes.body: To use an experience fragment, you add a reference to it in the Component Inspector. AEMaaCS automatically creates a new instance of the experience fragment in your page or component, inheriting its properties, which you can then modify as needed.

scenes.question: How do experience fragments improve reusability and maintainability?
scenes.heading: Avoiding duplicated code and ensuring components are consistent across the project
scenes.body: By using experience fragments, you can avoid duplicating code and ensure that your components are consistent across your project, improving both reusability and maintainability.
